Question: How do you deal with being rejected for a promotion you actually think you deserved?
Answer: I work with the Government of India. I will get my promotion only when my senior retires, which is 8 years from now. I will be eligible for it in 3.5 years. I will still have to wait another 4.5 years and there’s absolutely nothing I can do about it. So, I just accept the fact that there is. If I were in my previous job, it would have taken me around 25 to 30 years to reach where I am today. I could only get here because I tried to make a switch to a better position and it did require a lot of courage. We often tend to start feeling comfortable in a secure place. So, my way to deal with delayed promotions is to trying to do my best to get to a better position through hard work. I can leave it to time but I can also try harder. However, no pressure about it. Things take time. Luck also has to be on one’s side. I can’t affect all the factors but only the very few that are in my control. I’ll be happy if I get to a better place and even if I don’t. I have come to believe happiness has much little to do with designation than we assume.

Question: What are some harsh truth about Indian marriages?
Answer: My husband had to travel for work to Delhi. He had just one day of work but he decided to stay at his parent’s house for 4 days. I also got an opportunity to go to Delhi alone and since I’ll be on an official tour, I cannot extend my trip beyond my work requirements of two days. When I told my husband about this, he told me that I have to stay at his parent’s house at least for one day. The only question in my mind was: It is completely okay for him to not go meet my parent’s for even half an hour but if I go to our hometown, I have to necessarily be with his parents for a day. I don’t have any problems staying with his parents. They are good people. It’s just that I find this really unfair. This is as if more is expected out of me. Both of us stay very far off from our families. When we go back to our hometown, in every trip, I get to stay at my mom's home for 1–2 days at maximum . That makes it some 6–7 days in a year. I just think how many more times will I be able to meet my mom while she’s around and healthy? I can see her getting old and it really pains me. I miss her terribly. I call his mother every now and then and he hasn’t called mine (except her birthday) even once in 1.5 years of our marriage. Every time I bring up this topic, it only causes fights and problems like most other topics and the kind of person that I am, I’d rather be quiet than fight all day long. EDIT: The problem is amplified by people who believe in things like this: I am just asking for equality. The equality in expectations from both partners in a marriage and the acceptance of emotional needs of both partners. This is the problem with Indian marriages, we accept the “norms” without questioning them. My husband is not a bad person but feels bound by the norms too. It’s just sad.

Question: Do you feel protests and anger against Avadh Ojha and Vikas Divyakirti are justified?
Answer: I have been a regular to ORN for four years. My college was there. Then, I was a student at Vajiram & Ravi while preparing for UPSC during 2015–16. It is one of the most regretted decisions of my life. Now, this is what I have to say about my coaching experience. I lived with my family in Delhi so it was still better than my counterparts who lived in small dungeon-like rooms paying hefty rents and managing their food and chores. The coaching industry is just a money-making machine in ORN. I know a lot of successful people have passed out of there but so have thousands of unsuccessful ones, their stories are always unheard of. The civil services are hyped by this industry to a level where people believe if you are not an IAS, you are nothing and the failed aspirants are made to live their lives in regret. Very few people are able to truly move on from this dream they cultivate. The role of people like Avadh Ojha and Vikas Divyakirti is in hyping up the services, making sure people spend their hard-earned money and keep daydreaming. They make you believe that coming to Delhi and struggling there for years and years is the only way. I have seen so many failures including myself. This process breaks you from within. You are never the same again. These are the faces of the coaching industry which is making a fool out of several thousands and who will people end up blaming? These very faces only. It is high time we start looking the civil services and the role of coaching in a better light. We try to understand that coaching is neither a necessary nor a sufficient condition to make it through the exam. My honest opinion after being through the same lanes of ORN- Protests against the industry are justified. Students/aspirants need better facilities and what they pay for.

Question: Have you ever been mocked for your appearance?

When I started working, it gave me all the more incentive to look more presentable. I also got the money to invest more in the way I looked. I still get remarks on weight now that I am on the other side of the spectrum and greying hair. I have also been dealing with acne issue for quite some time now. Question: What is the selection process of the UPSC selection post recruitment?
Answer: Step 1: Scrutiny of the application is done by the UPSC to see if you meet the eligibility criteria (both education and/or experience) Step 2: A list of shortlisted candidates is published on the UPSC website and a chance is given to the un-shortlisted candidates to make representations if they think they should have been included. They can write and email to the UPSC. Step 3: The UPSC can hold a written examination for the post depending on the number of candidates. The written test is always followed by an interview. Else, there is only an interview. Step 4: UPSC conducts the interview at UPSC Bhawan, New Delhi. The scrutiny criteria is generally quite peculiar for specific posts and number of vacancies is also mostly quite low.

Question: What is the lifestyle of a civil servant?
Answer: This Sunday, I casually posted a photograph on my Instagram stories. One of my followers sent me this message in response: This made me realise that people have SO MANY misconceptions about the lifestyle of a civil servant. For that matter, even the term ‘civil servant’ Is associated with only bureaucrats thanks to the name of the examination conducted by UPSC (Civil Service Examination). Many people are under the impression that only IAS/IPS etc are “civil servants”. As a matter of fact, every person who works for the government in civilian capacity is a civil servant, governed by the Central Civil service Rules. Anyhow, talking about the lifestyle of civil servants. It generally depends on the rank and the choice. I have seen my bosses earning more than 2.5 lakh a month and still choosing to take the metro, not going on any holidays and saving every penny. I have seen peons and clerks saving up and/or taking EMIs to buy iPhones. The thing is: the pay is decent and stable. Obviously, at the starting level, managing in that income can be tough especially if someone has responsibilities but people who are on their own can easily lead a good lifestyle, depending on how you define it. Some people are frugal and careful with their money while some are ones who like to live in the moment. To each, his own. As for me, I wish to answer the question that the person on my Instagram story has posed: I can easily afford a Starbucks coffee every weekend or even more, if I want. I make pretty decent money. My gross salary is more than 1 lakh a month. I save a major chunk of rent by staying in government accommodation and paying HRA. I still do all shopping at discounts or from flea markets. The rest of the money is enough for me to manage home loan EMIs, car loan EMIs, SIPs, grocery and utility bills. Obviously the fact that my husband works and we have double income in our household really helps and we can save a major part of our combined income. To be honest, the things I cannot afford include foreign travel and that (when it happens) will be afforded by my husband because I spend my salary, run the household and he saves his salary for travel. If you ask me, my lifestyle has all elements that I wanted at this stage of life currently. It is all about making the best use of money that keeps you the happiest.

Question: What would you do if you fail in the UPSC after giving all the attempts?
Answer: I was extremely practical right from the beginning. I graduated in 2015, enrolled in UPSC coaching that completed in 2016. Wrote my first attempt in 2016 and figured I will not make it through the prelims stage. I started preparing for SSC CGL despite many doubts in my heart. The first one being it is only “group B” service and way below what I had set out to achieve. However, coming from a middle class family, I realise the importance of becoming independent and so I gave my shot at SSC CGL 2016 and cleared it. Meanwhile, I completed my post graduation in economics from IGNOU in 2017 and also cleared the entrance exam for LLB at University of Delhi. I also tried my luck at UPSC CSE prelims but again failed, this time by a short margin. I was pursuing LLB when the results for SSC CGL 2016 were announced. Since DU would not have allowed me to pursue the course part time and distance education is not recognised by the Bar Council of India- I again had a choice: I joined in May 2018. The nature of the job was such that I couldn’t keep pace with my UPSC preparation. I would also say that my motivation had somewhat died by then. After gaining some experience, I applied for a group A level 10 gazetted post through UPSC recruitment advertisement and bagged it. So, eventually, I did reach at a decent position. For those unaware, those selected in IAS also start at the same pay level as I did (level 10). However, the difference is that my promotions are very limited since it is an ex-cadre post. I may get just one promotion in my service to Deputy Director and depend on MACP to retire at the level of Director. This is my bittersweet story. Now, if you talk about UPSC CSE, I still have two attempts to go (owing to the age limit of 32). Sometimes, my mind wants to chase the dream for one last time but then my heart asks if this chase ever really ends? Everything has an opportunity cost. If I study with a full time job and a home to take care of, I have to sacrifice my family time, travel and bonding with my husband and even planning my family ahead. I never had enough money. Now that I have sufficient money, do I sacrifice the time? What is the surety I will be happy giving those attempts? Am I ready for that exam pressure at this age? So, tough choice. I just have to figure out what will make me happier and more importantly, keep me happier.

Name: Divya Sharma
Question: If you chose to write a book about your life, what would the title be?
Answer: When I joined my first job, I moved away from my family for the first time and started living alone. Everything had changed. It was a new city, entirely different from mine- different language, different climate, different problems and stark loneliness. It also came with a deep sense of guilt of doing nothing worthwhile in my life. I was told I had to go for tours and collect data from home to home in excruciating heat of 47–59 degrees every day for 19–25 days a month. That was my job. Nothing else. It was difficult and to be honest, embarrassing for me. I didn’t know how I should call my family and tell them that I became an “officer” who is getting some ₹38,000 per month and going door to door for a living. When I actually started going on tours, I saw the world with a new vision. My problems seemed so small. There were families who were surviving on ₹200 per day wage. They had no option to take a leave. They wouldn’t get paid. They had no weekends. They had no vacation. I saw deprivation. It pained me further. I listened to some stories everyday. I saw many stories everyday. Some said, some unsaid. After quite a few days of struggling with the food served by the tiffin service, I made some arrangement for cooking at my PG. I went to buy some utensils for the same. I asked the salesperson for a fork. Then suddenly, something hit my mind and I corrected myself, asking for two forks. The second fork symbolised a major change in my life that was about to come. I will just leave you to that. And in life, I had always had choices to make and just like a fork, each choice had different implications. It was not just the choice I was making but the implications I was accepting. …. And that has made all the difference. So, the title of the book on my life, which I know will never be written is- Two Forks.

Question: Why do new generation wives not prefer joint families?
Answer: I live with my husband in Bengaluru where I am posted. He works from home. It has been more than a year since we got married. We set up our home in Bengaluru from scratch together. Every little corner, every piece of furniture, appliance, utensils. This is our home. Nothing feels more like “ours” than this humble home we built together. We are have our own little family here which includes Capsicum and Maximum. Over the last one year, we have developed our ways of living together and developed routines that suit both of us. When we go back to our hometown for a week or so, every 2–3 months, we really enjoy our time there. We have a bigger family. We hang out together, go for dinners. There’s no routine. We enjoy the randomness there. However, we start missing our home after a point of time. We like the independence and the set of responsibility that comes with living on our own.

Question: Be honest, why do you write on Quora?
Answer: If I had to answer it in a sentence- I have a lot to say. I started writing on Quora way back in my college days (2014–15). I never had any social media accounts, like Orkut or Facebook while almost all of my school and college friends were connected on such platforms. I believe this is part of the reason why I lost touch with everyone. Actually, I was not even keen on staying in touch with them, now that I think of it. I had that urge of using social media and Quora was exactly that. I could write what I wanted and random strangers would read and upvote that. It gave me a wider scope. I gained quite a few followers back in the day and was ‘moderately popular’ by the then-standards. I would jump with joy when highly accomplished people like IITians, bureaucrats, famous writers would upvote my content or follow me. It gave me the validation that I always sought. However, I did realise that I was just wasting my time. These people are not real. They are just there on the internet and their validation will mean nothing in the long run if I don’t achieve something in my real life. I was spending hours and hours on Quora, checking every notification. This realisation made me permanently delete my first Quora account. I promised myself that I’ll come back only after I achieve something. I still didn’t have any social media account- no Facebook. I concentrated on my real world and when I cleared SSC CGL and entrance exam for DU LLB- I thought now is my time to finally indulge in something I had been craving. I started my second innings on Quora. I wrote about the exams and my experiences in my first job. Getting named as Top Writer 2018 gave me a boost. I kept writing. Cut to today, it has been over 6–7 years I have been writing on this platform, more regularly than I thought I would. I expanded this journey to making educational videos on YouTube last week. Only time will tell how it goes. I have a lot to say and when I write here, I feel I’m being heard.

Question: What would you advise to all from your marriage life? How happy/sad are you?
Answer: I’ll answer the second part first. Before I got married, I stayed with my family (father, mother and two sisters). I did not choose them. I lived with them because I was born in that family. I did not like all of them at all points in life. I had some issues and grudges with each one of them. Father is too controlling. Mother is too naive. Elder sister is too protective. Younger sister is too careless. Similarly, they had some issues with me. 90% of the times, we’d be all good but that 10% made us furious about each other. That’s how families are, right? We live away from each other and terribly miss all the time we spent together, even the fights and arguments. We would give anything to get a Time Machine to our childhood. Now, I’ll talk about my married life. I married someone I knew since I was barely 6 years old. We had been classmates since class 1 and best friends since 2008. He has been like family to me. And now he is my family. With him as well, none of the days are the same. Some days, he makes me really happy and I feel how lucky I am to be with him. Some days, I wish I had never married him to begin with and curl back into my shell. If you ask me I’m happy- one day, I’ll give you a big yes and the other day might be a sad no. So, my advice for married life is- let things flow. Just like you accept your family and love them with all your heart, without any conditions- do it for your spouse as well.

Question: Can you write something so deep that it would make me feel something?
Answer: Observe an Indian and a Pakistani in the west. There are numerous such YouTube channels/ artists which use the same label ‘brown’ in the west. Come to India/Pakistan. When you go up the ladder or think in a broader perspective, you find so many similarities and you identify with a common label. However, when you think of your daily life, you find ways to discriminate based on various grounds. These are just the two perspectives. At the broadest level, we are all just mortal human beings and being born and dying is the common factor to all of us. I always have this question then: why differentiate? What is the difference anyway?

Question: What is the coolest perk of any job you've had?
Answer: In my previous office, I was liked by my seniors, they appreciated my work a lot. My colleagues, however, despised me. They didn’t like when I was praised for my work. They had been there for quite a long time and may be felt threatened. I could sense this dislike/hate towards me. They wouldn’t say much but kept on ignoring me. I felt alone. All I would do was work and had practically no social life at office. I would see people my age hanging together and exploring places together while I would just be at my desk, except for one occasion. A cold vibe would enter the room with me. It went to the extent of all of them grouping against me in front of a senior, telling how bad of a person I am. I never talked ill or had any ill-intention for anyone. I was just doing my work with due diligence. I could see their faces when my book got published. You could see the jealousy in their eyes. Things took an evil turn when at least 6 of my ex-colleagues and 2 of my current colleagues competed for the same post that had a single vacancy. I got the job. This infuriated the ties further. No body turned up at my farewell. They expressed their hatred in more ways than one but it didn’t deter me. The story ended well when I sit here today, at a much better position. All they could do was be jealous and ignore me. May be, this turned in my favour as I didn’t go around having fun and instead concentrated on my future prospects and worked hard for it. I might have been stuck like them, loathing about the wasted time. The coolest perk of my job was that I only had to do my job and not care about petty issues. And still come out better. Most people cannot afford doing this- they get involved in petty office politics and gossip and ruin themselves. I am glad I could make the best out of my time.

Question: What was your most embarrassing airport/airplane experience?
Answer: I was on an official tour from Delhi to Ahmedabad and had an early morning flight to catch. It was just a few hours after India had lost the Cricket World Cup final in Ahmedabad. I knew I had a long day ahead of me as I had to head straight to the event venue and could back to the hotel room very late (around 11 PM). I was worried how I would carry on my day with the state I was in. I just hoped not to make any more blunders for the next few days due to lack of sleep.

Name: Divya Sharma
Question: What do you want to tell people your age?
Answer: Yesterday was International Women’s Day. My office was kind enough to organise a get together to congratulate the women at the workplace. They had also planned on playing a fun game. The kind where one has to keep tossing a balloon in the air while making a glass pyramid. I was called to play with another employee. She said if she loses “beizzati ho jaegi”. It will be shameful if she loses. Even when said jokingly, I see this temperament a lot more these days. People are becoming increasingly competitive, even where they are just supposed to let lose and have fun. There is so much anxiety, so many ‘what if’s’ and these very what if’s stop people from even trying for things they want. I get so many messages almost everyday where (mostly) aspirants keep telling me they are in a spiral- they can’t study because they are anxious and they are anxious because they can’t study. This emanates from that feeling of “beizzati ho jaegi”. I will be honest- even I have gone through this phase but I will tell you something that helped me out of it: You are not as important as you think you are. The world is not staring at you and hoping for you to win. Most of the people won’t even bat an eye for your success or failure. Your success or failure is your own. There is no “beizzati” or shame in trying for things you want. The worst case is you will lose. The best case is you will win. All of it belongs to you. How many times in a day do you think about what others are doing? so, again, I want to tell you: You are not as important as you think you are. Don’t think about what others will think. They have better things to do.

Name: Divya Sharma
Question: I am currently working as a TA-CBDT through CGL 2022. I am enjoying the work and office environment but also worried about the new RR. Should I consider CGL 2024 exam, targeting 4600/4200 GP posts?
Answer: I’ve been observing so many people in my current workplace as well who have joined at an entry-level post, earning pretty less for a metro city, having great potential to do better but just settling for their low-paying jobs because they are comfortable. I will tell you something. 1. There is no problem at all in being comfortable. If you see a future in your current workplace as peaceful and are happy being a frog in a well, unwilling to explore other options, go ahead, stay there. There are many within the government set up. Do whatever makes you happy. 2. Workplace environment is largely guided by the people in that environment. The people you are working with right now might be very good but you know, no one is permanent. Some will retire, some will get transferred, go on deputation etc and the work environment won’t stay the same forever. So, it is wrong to trust the work environment to be constantly good and staying in a place for long just for that. 3. As explained in above point, the scenario can change anytime and as in your case, RR have changed. You have an example right in front of you. Now, just imagine, the scenario has changed and you can do nothing about your job since you have exhausted your age limit to apply elsewhere. Now, you will live the rest of your time in deep regret. You will keep thinking how you had the time with you and you didn’t make a move just because you were comfortable. You will see others making a lot of money and you and your family will be just making ends meet. raising kids and affording a comfortable lifestyle isn’t cheap. Think about the long term. So, if you are not in category 1 of the points above, please study and make your life better. at least, give it a try. Be comfortable now or be more comfortable in the future- the choice is yours to make.

Name: Divya Sharma
Question: Why don’t women want to be wives anymore?
Answer: While speaking to someone, I told how I am much relaxed. Whenever I am tired or have some other tasks at hand, I tell my husband and he prepares dinner even before I reach home. He works from home and his shift ends around 5. Also, he enjoys cooking. On most days, I prepare dinner or we share the workload. He can make the curry, I can make rotis/rice, salad and set the table. The man I was talking to responded by saying that he knows how to cook but not by any chance will he cook if someone asks him to. He told how only his wife, who is also working, cooks at home. This is just a small example of how women are entrusted to play certain roles like cooking and looking after the household even while their roles have evolved and a lot of women now step out of the house and work. It is because of such pre conceived notions that most independent women don’t wish to set in the role of a ‘wife’ as believed in the popular sense of the term. If you tell them that they can be a wife who will have an understanding partner who treats her like an equal, most would be happy doing the same.

Name: Divya Sharma
Question: What is the greatest act of cruelty you have ever committed?
Answer: I never let my younger sister buy expensive pens like V5, Trimax that I used to get occasionally and told her that she can buy expensive pens the day she improves her handwriting. I didn’t even remember this till my sister, who is now 26, reminded me of this. She had visited me in Bengaluru and looking at my pen stand reminded her of this. I love my sister dearly. I did not even remember doing something cruel to her as a kid that has had a lasting impact on her that she still remembers it. She was an average student while I had been the ‘topper’ kind. We went to the same school. She often talks about how our teachers would repeatedly compare her with me and won’t even spare our mother during Parent-Teacher’s meetings. My mother was mature enough to always tell them that all fingers are not the same. I was clearly not mature enough. I was probably pushing her to do better using similar motivation tools like expensive pens that motivated me. I can say that for sure that I did not have any ill-intention. I apologised to her. I am genuinely apologetic. I should not have treated her that way. I had no right to do that. I could pull off that just because I made her feel she didn’t deserve something and she never even asked for it. She did go on to score 90% in class 12 and that surprised everyone. She had really worked hard that time. I don’t know what motivated her. These small acts by elders that children face, make them feel insecure and they cannot forget such things even when they are all grown up. I have explicitly learnt too lessons from this- I cannot turn back time but I wish I could. I am really sorry. I didn’t mean to cause any hurt.

Name: Divya Sharma
Question: Can I give a good life to my family through government jobs?
Answer: I was probably in school when my mother told me how my father had once pointed out at the famous Parikrama Restaurant in Central Delhi. The 240-feet-high restaurant is considered to be very posh and romantic since it gives you the view of the entire city while revolving. With due course of time, they had forgotten about it. A middle class family could not even think of going there, it is quite expensive. Let alone that restaurant, we hardly went out for any dinners like other families. The most we would do sometimes when mom was not well was to order from the local restaurant and that too was a rarity because we would then have something quick like khichdi. Father had a confectionery shop and evenings were the busiest time of the day. He would not take a day off Few years later, when we got a chance, I treated my family at that very restaurant on my sister’s birthday. My parents were delighted. So was I. Once while traveling in a DTC bus, my mom looked out of the window and said, there are so many houses, I wish one of these was ours. I did buy a home after living in rented houses for over 14 years. My sisters helped me. From the smallest desires to big ones, I have been trying to give my family a good life. We are happy with what we have because it is all we had wished for once. Desires never end but we should be grateful for what we could achieve at our own pace. So, yes, you can give a good life to your family with a government job. What matters is your definition of ‘good’.

Name: Divya Sharma
Question: What is it like to be raised by an Indian/Pakistani mother?
Answer: A recent sweet gesture by my mother made me search for the question and it turned out I already had an unpublished draft answer written at least 3 years ago. So, I’ll be posting both today. Mind you, we are 26 and 29 respectively and our mother had just one response to the video: Were you scared? My heart melted. She is so sweet. Only a mother can think like this. 2. My mother, like always, gets really excited when I’m about to come home. And this time was an all of a sudden plan so she was even happier. She called me a few days ago and was very excited to tell me: “Deebu, Maine Bohot paise Jod ke rakhe hai. Tu aaegi toh Hum khoob khaane peene chalenge.” Deebu, I’ve saved a lot of money, we’ll go out and eat a lot when you come back. I thought she had stopped saving after my sisters and I had started working. Anyway, I asked her how much she had saved. She replied with even more excitement: “₹ 1400” I can’t even explain how I felt at that moment. ₹1400 is a lot for her. She is just so adorable. My eyes well up everytime I think about her getting old.

Name: Divya Sharma
Question: What is that one thing that has completely changed your views about a person or community?
Answer: A definitely controversial answer but I’m in the mood today. So, let’s do it. My views about reservation to SC/ST in government institutions and jobs have changed. Growing up, I had always heard caste-based reservation is bad and unfair. It eats up into ‘our’ category seats. When I was in college, I remember how we could ‘identify’ quota girls just by looking at few of them. They used to form their own groups. We never mingled with them and they didn’t either. When I started preparing for government jobs, the feeling was reinforced because everywhere I used to see people saying that we get only 50% of the seats. The year Tina Dabi became the topper, I was so furious because I couldn’t clear the prelims cut off of UPSC exam and could have easily done it had I been from the reserved section and May be could have even topped the exam like she did. This was not equality. She gets a chance to prove herself in the mains and interview even while doing not that good in the prelims and I don’t. Objective answers have never been my strength and I couldn’t get past the prelims stage only. The one thing that completely changed my view was when I started working and actually went out in the rural nooks and corners of the villages in one of the most backward regions of our country. As a part of my job, I saw their homes, the kind of work they are expected to do and get to do. The most important factor is the social backwardness. I don’t even know how to describe it but I urge you to go and feel it. They are still not completely accepted into the society. I started thinking deeply about it and my views evolved there on. Then I looked back in time and realised that this was just not about rural India, it is also about big cities like Delhi where I grew up. I started connecting the dots. Let me admit here. Even I was one of the people who used to socially outcast people coming from the reserved section. However, my apprehension was typically characterised by what I used to hear- they are undeserving and they get our seats. They could get what I got in half the effort that I did. They are just not my level. So, for me, caste-based reservation was the cause of discrimination, not the caste per-se. I have known so many people all my life and more so when I started working, who don’t need reservations to discriminate. They will just discriminate. It is because of such people that reservation is needed. I just want you to look into yourself, as you read this answer, and think about this- You will get the answer on why we need reservation. Just to clear a few things here- The major factor here are the examples like the Dabi sisters- people whose previous generations have taken full advantage of the system and have come to the forefront. We ask the question- why do they still use reservation to get around? Well, the answer lies here- They are still identified by their caste. They always will be. So, they might as well use their caste to get where they want. Even if some of them are interested to go all out and fight it out without using their certificates, they can still be sure that almost everyone is going to ask their full names and judge them for it. I want you to keep an open mind to this and really think about it.

Question: As an Indian, if you don't believe in God, then how truly do you follow the rituals/customs/fasts (vrat) your in-laws ask you to do?
Answer: I don’t believe in God per se but I do believe in culture. For me, going to the temple/gurudwara, keeping fasts, customs, wearing traditional symbols like mangalsutra and sindoor are all part of my culture. So, I am not against any of that. I enjoy festivities and customs and truly look forward to all of it. It is much beyond my belief in god. And for that matter, I would like to tell you that I grew up in a typical Brahmin, very religious family. We had all sorts of rules. My in-laws are 10 times more chill than the family I was born in. They don’t ask me to do anything. I do it out of respect for them and their religious/cultural inclination. I consider fasting to be just another day of intermittent fasting followed by getting all dressed up. I like it and do it with all my heart :) This was my mehendi from my first karva chauth.

Name: Divya Sharma
Question: What is one food you'll never eat?
Answer: The only time I have said this sentence after eating something for the first time was for a hot dog. For the starters, I always thought that all hot dogs are like the aloo tikki or veg patty hot dogs that I used to get at small shops in the neighbourhood. However, very recently, at a movie theatre, I tried an actual hot dog. The sausage was something I could not even hold in my mouth. I wished to run and throw it away. I had never tasted anything so awful. The texture of the sausage was making me feel giddy. Even typing this is making me feel like I’ll puke. Such a famous street snack and I cannot understand how and why. I sworn that day that I will never have it again. I have been a vegetarian all my life and started having non veg only very recently after my marriage. It is understandable that I still have not developed the taste for all of it. It is all very new for me. Never giving the hot dog a chance again though.

Question: What does your typical workday look like?
Answer: My typical workday starts with freshening up and hitting the gym. Then I prepare some breakfast and pack fruit for office. I leave for work. It takes me a 35–40 mins drive. At my work place, I don’t usually get any targets. On some days, there’s a lot of work that I don’t get time to even look up or eat and some days, there’s hardly any work. I come to office and typically take a look at the white board across my table. There’s a list of tasks to be completed and delegated. It helps me keep a track of work. Then I begin with my day. If it is a low volume day, I read the newspaper or write answers on Quora. I typically take 2 breaks- one for the fruit of the day and the other for some snack, some roasted dry fruits or chana. I keep a stack of such snacks in my drawer. I don’t have tea or coffee or a proper lunch. This helps me maintain my weight and I don’t really feel hungry during office hours. I head back in the evening between 5:30–6. I immediately start preparing dinner as I reach home. On some days, if it’s non-veg, my husband cooks and I only relax. Dinner is done by 7:30 or 8 max if it is something fancy. Then we usually go for a walk and run errands. I read newspaper if I had not been able to during the day. The good habit I have been able to inculcate now is to fall asleep as soon as I hit the bed. The key is to not use phone. I just close my eyes and fall into deep sleep in a few minutes. I am mostly fast asleep by 10–10:30 PM.

Question: How's your life going on at the moment?
Answer: Once I was talking to someone when they asked me about my experience with my mother-in-law and sister-in-law. I said I have no complaints. Then I said a few good words about them. That person was taken aback and told me that I am too positive about it and even if I am, I should not say it out loud because nazar lag jaegi. (You will attract evil eye) I smiled at it and thought to myself that mostly when people have their life going good, they often don’t talk about it— mostly because they think they will jinx it. As they say, we have some things we really wished for and once we have them, we forget how much we wished for them. So, it is just soul satisfying for me to be grateful to the things I currently have- So, yes, life is mostly good. I can’t complain about a lot of good things that I have right now. Obviously, there are some negative aspects too but we will leave that for now. Just one negative that bothers me the most is being missing my family and home all the time. Question: What happened to you today that was completely unexpected?

Question: What was the best relationship advice you ever got?
Answer: Don’t raise your volume. As my mother puts it: When you have to put across a point, you can always do it politely. It will be more effective. When one maintains respect even while they fight, the other person also usually follows. I learnt this from my mother. She always taught us to be calm. Another reason I learnt this was during most of the fight between my parents, my mother maintained her demeanour always and it genuinely helped their ailing relationship. Father would also eventually understand. This is very simple yet very effective way to act mature and sail through the problems in any relationship.

Name: Divya Sharma
Question: Don't you regret pursuing an MA from IGNOU rather than some top DU college?
Answer: I am working in a top government position (group A gazetted) which required an MA degree in Economics. I could get the job after an interview with the UPSC and competing against my experienced colleagues from the top colleges. If I look back in time, I would have passed out of a ‘top’ college in 2017 and then I would have started writing competitive exams. If luck were to be on my side, I would have started working in say, 2019, considering the delays in joining. This in itself would have taken me a year back in my career from where I am right now. While pursuing my masters from IGNOU, I could not only learn Economics but also had the time and energy to: a. learn various other subjects and a lot about our country and the World while I prepared for UPSC CSE and SSC CGL. b. earn money by teaching school and college students at home and that helped me revise the syllabus and be up to date. To be honest, it was only after the UPSC selected me with my MA from IGNOU degree, I hold no regrets. Before this, I was sceptical about it. I know some people might think it isn’t valid for private jobs but I never wanted to do one. So, not been a problem for me. Also, if someone is capable enough, they can land the job. Name: Divya Sharma
Question: How has 2023 been for you?
Answer: I wish to note down month-wise major happenings of the year. May be some years down the lane, when I read this answer, it will make me smile. January- I went for my first trip with a group of strangers to Gokarna. It was a very different experience for me. I spent a night looking at the stars at a beach, nothing short of magic. I connected with myself. It was so relaxing. I stayed away from any screen and unnecessary noise in my head. February- I got married. It was a bittersweet feeling. Though I was living away from my family, officially moving away from them made me really emotional. I moved into another family and have a new set of parents now. I have many more responsibilities. March- I traveled to one of my dream destinations- Kashmir. It was actually like a dream, so serene and so beautiful. It is truly heaven on Earth. Met really sweet people. Also spent a few days in my in-law’s house and enjoyed the new bahu phase. April- I was invited by a coaching institute to give a talk on my career and guide the students. It was another thing that I always wanted to do. I had taught and guided thousands of students virtually but doing that in person was something I will always cherish. May- I went for my first work trip as Assistant Director to Diu. It was such a nice experience. I got more respect, something I yearned for being a group B officer. When you at a lower post, you just look up and want to do better. I was finally feeling the way I always wished. Obviously, I wish to go higher but I am so grateful for what I had and what I have now. June- I got my first car. Now this was not even in my wildest dreams but somehow, we felt the need for a lifestyle upgrade. I had added another life-skill, I learnt how to drive. It is so liberating to be free to move anywhere I wish. July- It was another work trip to Mahabalipuram. Meanwhile, we were moving away from the newly-married phase to setting up a house and owning up responsibilities. Every few days felt like new. There was constant change. August- We went to Delhi for my birthday and I threw a barbie-themed party for near ones, only to regret later looking at the bill amount. I remember writing a quora answer about the same. September- My sister and brother-in-law came to Bengaluru and I had my first road trip in my car with them. Driving for about 200 km at a stretch on the highway with blasting music and everyone singing along was such an experience. I can never forget that. Every moment from that trip is so precious. October- It was the month when my best friend gave birth to her daughter, Jisha. I remember how I cried happy tears the day she gave me the news of her pregnancy. When I finally held her in my arms, I got all answers to the questions I had. I always wondered why people make such a big deal out of having kids and being a mother. I can not wait to watch her grow up. November- My first Karva Chauth, diwali after marriage- good time with family. I also got the chance to work at Delhi office for some 15 days and attend a global conference in Ahmedabad. I also got to know more about the scope of fisheries in the country. It is a lesser known but an immensely important sector. December- Lastly, I went to attend a destination wedding in Kerala. Had another road trip with friends for the New Year’s and mostly, had a lot of fun. Among all these good parts that I would like to take away from this year, I also need to acknowledge certain negative emotions I felt. I was not alone anytime of the year but I did feel lonely and lost at times. I still have a few regrets and wanted to work towards some betterment. I kept procrastinating the entire year, almost. This is just adding to regret. This year, 2024, I will try not to accumulate any regrets. I will learn another life-skill: the art of saying no. I will stand up for myself and things that I wish to achieve. I have enough time and I don’t have enough time- It all depends on how I choose to spend my time. If I am on the right path, I hope I write a better answer to such a question next year around this time.

Question: Smriti Irani opposed by menstrual paid leaves) what is your opinion?
Answer: There have been numerous times when I get my period just before leaving for work or during work. I mostly throw a few tantrums or may be just shed a tear out of pain and emotional distress, but then it is fine. It has been several years since I have been menstruating and I have learnt to deal with it somehow. I don’t pop in pain killers too because I know the pain subsides in a few hours and mild cramps can even take two days. However, one of my friends, has PCOD. She gets extremely painful periods which are not even regular. She feels nauseous and spends at least one full day vomiting. She has to necessarily take pain killers. Worst part, she is not even prepared for it most of the times. One of the other friends who has not been diagnosed with PCOD or any other hormonal issues, still faces painful periods with nausea and has a tough time going to work. So, you see, women face menstruation differently. There is no black and white here. While I agree menstruation is not a handicap, it is certainly a pressing issue for many women. My opinion is to work out a middle way. Paid menstrual leaves is not the solution since it drastically affects the preference for females as employees. The companies might think of options like work-from-home or may be, compensating for lost hours of work on weekends or flexible working hours so that women can at least choose their convenience without the employer suffering much loss.

Question: What was the most dangerous decision you were about to take but later avoided?
Answer: Quitting my government job. It was May 2019. It had been a year into my job as Junior Statistical Officer in a small town called Akola in Maharashtra. I have written a lot about in the past. For the uninitiated, my job was to go door to door and conduct various surveys. It was physically and mentally taxing. Anyway, I was preparing for UPSC CSE along with the job in the very little time I could get in the evenings/off days. It was increasingly stressful. My health was also not great owing to the tough nature of the job. I was supposed to write the UPSC CSE prelims that year in the same month. As fate would have it, I was deployed to work in Nagpur FOD office for reasons I cannot disclose here. The period of deployment was also not made clear to me. Anyway, I was working hard in 48 degrees hot summer every day. I had to walk 10 Kms everyday for a sample in a small remote village for 4–5 days. Then, I got a sample in one of the poshest areas of Nagpur- where all the biggies live. Luxury cars like porsche and Mercedes were a common sight in the parking lots of those mansion-like buildings. But one fine day, in that posh area, a man made a move on me and I was lucky I could escape that situation. I was all alone and I still remember, sitting down on the footpath and crying like a mad woman. I cannot write why I did not tell my office about this incident else people will come to teach me conduct rules in the comments. Only I know how I felt that day. The man even told me how he could pay me if I was ready for it. He told it to my face. If I am going door to door in this scorching summer, I can do almost anything for money. I was taken aback. That evening, I called my father and asked him if we were in a position financially so that I could leave this job. I did not tell him what happened that day. My father asked me not to leave the job and I did not. And I also let go of my dream of becoming an IAS officer that very day.

Name: Divya Sharma
Question: What is the worst thing parents can do to their children?
Answer: I made a mistake when I was in class 12 and that mistake was sneaking out on a lunch date with my boyfriend. That is it. A lunch. Anyway, I was too scared to tell and did not tell my family but they somehow go to know. The consequence? My mother slapped me some 10–15 times, I don’t even remember. I was so numb. And I was grounded. My mother, my sisters, nobody would even talk to me. I was made to feel so guilty. I used to just be in my room and cry. There were strict rules imposed on me. I did not have any friends even. So, I was terrible. It was too much to take for me. I would feel all dark and gloomy and most importantly, very lonely. My ‘mistake’ was successfully hidden from my father. The consequences would have been worse, I am sure. I had my board exams in a few days and all with all that mental pressure and bad behaviour I was receiving at home, I severely underperformed. I was expected to top the school since I had been the topper for years. I couldn’t get my dream college. I had to settle for an off campus college and that insecurity of not being able to study from a Campus college in Delhi still haunts me. I tell people that I passed out from University of Delhi. They would ask which college? I answer with Janki Devi Memorial College and the conversation always turns awkward because most people haven’t even heard of it. Some even have believed that I have made up the name. So, this regret always stays with me. The worst thing that parents can do to their children is not forgiving them. Only if my mother would have understood me and forgiven me at the right time, I might have not screwed up my board exams and may have studied from a college that I wanted. She anyway did come around when I started going to college and I kept thinking what if she had come around at the right time and saved a major part of my life. This is just one incident. I landed up in a lot of trouble because of that guy during school days. Thankfully, he had a gala time because the parents of a boy don’t really worry much. For girls, it is all about the family’s honour. To give you some climax to this story, I married the same guy 11 years later after several ups and downs.

Question: What beauty standard has affected you the most?

I struggled a lot during my teenage years because I have very sensitive skin and waxing was the only option back then. It was only after I started working, I learnt the importance of being well groomed all the time and now it doesn’t even feel like a hassle. Name: Divya Sharma
Question: How many Indian guys here have not asked for a dowry, and what were your reasons?
Answer: My boyfriend of several years proposed me in 2020. We had not particularly discussed marriage but it was kind of obvious. Things did go a little south after that but one fine day, his mother called both of us on a conference call and asked us to give a definite date to get married. Both of us had different apprehensions. We were not ready for the big step yet. My major apprehension was that we did not have enough money for the wedding. Even for my elder sister’s marriage, we could barely spend anything. That is another story, I will write about it someday. We are three sisters and our father did not save anything for our wedding in the name of dowry. He ensured we get good education. So, as was planned, I went on to buy a flat for my parents in April 2022. All my savings and some of my sisters’ went into that big purchase. Now, many would say I could have saved that money for the wedding but I was so sure that giving my parents a safe home is much more important than feeding guests for two days who have done absolutely nothing for me. In May 2022, his parents invited us for dinner and gave me a gold chain. It was a surprise. Things were finally getting real. Now that the wedding was on the cards and as it is expected for the bride’s side to host the wedding party, we expressed our inability. I could only propose taking another personal loan. I had no other option with my salary back then. I could not expect money from my father and even my sisters. Father had a small business on the verge of being shut down and his health was only deteriorating with time. So, forget about dowry, my father-in-law was kind and generous enough to host the wedding function entirely out of his money. He was against me taking any further loans and understood my situation. I still did pay for a sangeet-mehendi function that we hosted and gifts for the groom’s family. So, yes, there are people out there who are willing to support you. I am thankful to my father-in-law and mother-in-law. I bought this lehanga from the royalty amount of my first book :) It came as a surprise. There were so many little elements that we put together with very little money and so many tears :’)

Name: Divya Sharma
Question: What is your most expensive gift (gifted by yourself)?
Answer: I drove to the Service Centre to give my car for a free service this morning. At the Service Centre, I opened Uber App and chose the cheapest way to reach my office- an uber bike. During the ride, I was thinking about this. This is how I am wired, I suppose. I try to save on almost every possible expense. I can hardly remember a time when I booked a cab ride just for myself or ate at a really nice restaurant alone. If I have company, I don’t hesitate a bit. When it comes to spending on myself- I feel guilty. I used to be very passionate about shopping back in the day but even that is dying down. I will buy anything new only when the older thing has worn out completely. I hardly have a few pairs of clothes and shoes now. I have bought quite a few expensive things with my money: a house, a car and iPhone. None of that actually made me feel as if I have achieved something great. Every responsible adult tries to meet certain materialistic needs. I really feel special when on certain days, I give myself little treats. These are a few things that I really enjoy/like but rarely do because I feel guilty of spending money just on myself. It might not be the most expensive thing but treating myself better, prioritizing my needs and occasionally loving myself without guilt is the most special gift.

Question: What is the best reason someone has given you for why they do not want children?

Answer: Going to my mother’s home. I was posted in Bangalore two months before my wedding. But now, it feels so bad when I land at the Delhi airport and don’t get to see my mother even in 2–3 days. It kills me from inside when I have to “seek” time to meet her. My mother-in-law was appreciating me for spending only one night at my parents’ after my wedding. No one really stops me actually but I feel torn between the (unsaid) expectations my in-laws have and the way I miss my mother. No one tells me that I shouldn’t go to my mother’s place so often but when we come back for just 3–5 days, I am expected to be around for my husband and my in-laws. This time during Diwali, I made sure I balance this out since we were home for some 15 days but still, I stayed at my mom’s for two nights on two different weekends and that is when I truly felt I am on a vacation. I feel free. I feel so loved. I feel so much love for my parents and sisters. Just the day I landed in Bangalore, I got a call from my office that I have to be on an official trip to Delhi for a few days, I couldn’t be happier. My husband tagged along. I was in Delhi on Tuesday and due to workload, I couldn’t visit my mother till Friday evening. But when I did, I stayed back and came back to my in-law’s on Saturday evening. My husband was clearly not happy with me because I am supposed to leave for another city for a few days for official purpose and I decided to spend a weekend away. However, I have promised myself now that I won’t let it bother myself now. I should not feel guilty for choosing myself once in a while. I do almost everything for him and my new family now. A new relationship should not mean giving less importance to the old ones. Even being married, I should have the right to do what makes me feel happy and fulfilled. I will do what truly makes me happy: seeing my family. That’s the least and the most that I want in life.

Question: What is the best marriage advice you would give to me if I will be married in a month so our relationship will be strong physically, emotionally, and in terms of longevity, and what are some common marital mistakes that I can avoid in our marriage?
Answer: I have been feeling under the weather lately. My husband walked in with a book to read at night. I started talking. He tried to read but since I kept talking, he made a little face, kept the book down and started listening to me. I was sharing some feelings I had before marriage and how stressful was all of that for me- it still gives me chills. I had to manage every single detail and being a bride, I was out arranging things to the last minute. I don’t talk about these things to anyone and I just wanted to share. After a little while, he looked at me and asked me for how long I will keep talking and was upset that he couldn’t read. Ugh, I felt deeply guilty. I stopped talking immediately. He left the room to read in the living room, I turned on the TV and while the TV played in the background, I started thinking about it. What would have I done if I were in his place? I am in his place a lot of times when I am engaged in my own chores but he has to talk and even subconsciously, I don’t concentrate on my chores and listen to him 100%. So many of the times, I don’t understand a thing because it’s mostly some scientific fact or some random movie or TV show I never watched. I still try to listen. Then it hurt me a little. After some more thinking, I realised what I do is completely my choice and I do it involuntarily. I don’t force myself to listen to him. I do because I feel the need to be heard so I know how it feels not to be heard and I try listening to him. Not just him, this stands for every person I love. The only point that hurts me is the question: What would have I done if I were in his place? Every time I ask myself this question, it hurts deeply. Why? Because I expect. Why and how can I expect people to behave the way that I do and treat me the way I treat them? They are their own person. They are involuntarily choosing what is important to them, just like I do. Just like me. The only difference is that sometimes that priority will not be me and I have to learn to be okay with that. I cannot force people. I rather should not. I have seen the consequences in the past. I felt calmer after talking to myself and now I will always try to stop talking even when he implies with his actions. My only advice being married for about 8 months- accept people for who they are and bet they would be different from you. Don’t expect to be treated the same way. Marriage will change you in ways you never expect.

I have never seen her getting love from her husband. Now that I am married, I realise it more- how important is the love of the husband for a woman. I feel so helpless now. The helplessness makes me cry.

Question: What is the most soul-satisfying thing you have ever done in your life that left you with a sense of contentment and peace within yourself?
Answer: I have written about it before but I wish to write about it again. My grandfather was a clerk in a government department. With four children, he could barely make ends meet. My father was the eldest son. He started working at the age of 14, even went street to street on his bicycle to sell milk etc. He ran his shop for several years and built a home for us. Things changed, he faced a major financial setback, thanks to some poor rushed decisions, and we lost everything- including our home. We lived in different rented homes for more than 14 years. I am sorry to say but we as tenants did face a lot of discrimination like higher maintenance fees, no membership or say in the society board and the occasional taunts by neighbourhood uncles and aunties. One day, I was going in the DTC bus with my mother. She was looking out of the window and said “I always think there are thousands and lakhs of homes. I wish there was one among these for us as well.” That sentence hit me. I saved up all that I could and with the help of my sisters, I could finally fulfil our long lost dream- our own home. There have been so many struggles and so many sacrifices to make that happen. I was even faced with this challenge when people told me that it would be a problem in my marriage because no one would accept a daughter-in-law who has an ongoing loan and almost full responsibility of taking care of her parents even after the marriage. The society is not very favourable for the couple who has no male child. But I did it. I did not worry about my marriage. It was not the time to be selfish. I was sure that the person who truly loves me will accept me with my responsibilities. I was not asking anyone to pay for my parents. I am capable enough to take care of them. This is the most soul satisfying feeling in my life. I am so glad my parents are spending their old age in their own home, with all the luxuries that we could afford. It truly makes me feel content and at peace. This photo was taken on 19th April, 2022- the day the flat was registered in my name and we had some Nirula’s to celebrate. I can still feel the goosebumps.

Question: What secrets are you hiding from your parents?
Answer: This can be really embarrassing for me but I want to get it out of my system. When I was posted in Akola, Maharashtra, I fell really sick. It started off as cold and cough, presumably due to weather change. As in most Indian households, I did not go to see a doctor immediately. However, it got much worse than I had expected. My throat had swelled up badly and my ears were paining excruciatingly. I felt as if my hearing abilities have drastically reduced. It was then that I visited an ENT specialist. He told me that I should have visited him earlier and I had just aggravated a simple issue of sinusitis due to carelessness. There is some blockage in my ear and I was on the verge of damaging my right ear permanently. I could sense the truth in his words. I could feel the pain. I came out of the clinic and just at the gate of the clinic, I searched on google if a person who is deaf from one ear could get any relaxation in the UPSC exam. Such was my mental state at that point in time that I felt like a big zero- a big failure. My parents, especially my father, had only one dream for me and I could not achieve it and kept failing. I had a central government job and I was just so desperate. The thought of being a failure was making me feel as if I am sinking. I would sit down to study but the fear of failure won’t let me do it. I would stare at the books for hours and cry. I am sure a lot of other aspirants have felt this way at some point. Some were able to fight off the fear and win the battle while others, like me, succumbed to it and gave up the preparation altogether. I gave up because I could not take it any longer. The failure was affecting my mental health to the extent of self-harm and I bet my parents would rather see me alive and healthy. Somedays, it still irks me. I still cry. I want to fight my fears and I hope, someday, I do.

Question: Are only Class 1 officer (IAS, IPS) serving the nation or is there some contribution from lower class employees also?
Answer: I worked as a Group B non-gazetted Officer (erstwhile Class II) for more than four years in two different departments. Currently, I have been working as a group A gazetted Officer (erstwhile Class I) for about 9 months. During this journey, I have come across several other Group A, B, C employees and from the so-called prestigious cadres too. All I have understood is that each person has a role to play and that role is important in its own sense. You need a watchman to guard a building. You need a sweeper to keep the building clean. You need a peon to open the locks every morning. You need a clerk to do the routine tasks. You need a group B officer to do all the drafting work. You need a group A officer to take the risks of her decisions and accountability for the actions of her team. At every level, the responsibility is divided and accountability is ensured. It hurts me when only the top brass gets all the credit just like the actors in a movie and the entire crew of the movie gets none of the acknowledgment. Some people run the show with the help of many others.

Question: How do you know how physically attractive you actually are?
Answer: I had always been a very skinny person till I was 20. Skinny to the extent that I considered myself ugly. I had no glow on my face. I was very insecure about the way I looked. Plus, I am just about 5’2–5’3. My petite frame made me a good source of jokes for my classmates sometimes. Thanks to many bottles of glucose that were pumped into my body for a period of 6 days when my platelet levels hit down to 18,000 in 2014, I could finally gain some weight. After college, I started paying more attention to the way I looked. I anyway didn’t have much money to spend on clothing and accessories. I would mostly get hands me down from my elder sister and new clothes only on very special occasions. It was then that I started getting many compliments on my looks, more in person because I was not on any social media platform, thanks to my insecurities. I am currently 3 kgs below my highest-ever-weight. Like many others, the work from home regime during covid gave me a head start and since then I have been having a tough time controlling my weight. For the past few months, I have been getting many comments on my weight on social media. It has made me feel really conscious. Since I have been on both ends of the spectrum- the only conclusion I could draw out of it was- there will be phases of being ‘physically attractive’ and I need to appreciate that. I cannot be physically attractive all the time. I have to work for it. Obviously, we get a few things naturally but maintaining that physical form is tough in itself. I have been working out, trying to keep my stress levels low, getting good sleep and eating healthy. I know it is just a phase and I’ll be back in shape. So, I don’t know how physically attractive I am but I am definitely trying to be.

Question: How did you fall in love with yourself?
Answer: Yesterday in the evening itself, my office organised a small belated birthday celebration for me. I told about myself. Last night, I was finding it so hard not to cry. I was feeling extremely anxious. I was making up scenarios in my head- some of which might actually turn out to be true. Question: What are the best and worst feelings in the world?

Question: What is your motivation to work?
Answer: I still remember how I used to make excuses to avoid my friends coming to my home. Our family of five and a pet dog lived in a small 2BHK rented apartment which had walls full of seepage. The room that we three children shared was quite small. I started teaching as soon as I passed class 12. My first income was Rs. 1400/- after teaching two kids for a month and I gave in my contribution to buy my sister a guitar. She really wanted to learn that. I kept teaching and providing for some of the ‘luxuries’ like new clothes for my mother and ourselves. I still remember how my elder sister gave most part of her salary to meet the household expenses and towards the education of our younger sister. I also followed suit when I joined my job. My heart would always be prepared for any random call from my father asking for money. I would save every penny that I could. I would prefer walking and public transport over private vehicles and general/sleeper class over AC classes in trains wherever possible. I would even cut down expenses on food. I had two meals for Rs. 25/- each everyday. My motivation to work is simple- The bills. I will be bluntly honest. I am working so that I can make money and take care of my family and lead a good lifestyle myself. I love to see how far we have come as a family. My parents proudly reside in a big enough 2 BHK+ study apartment in a good society. I drive my own car. I have been able to visit home more often and afford air tickets. I pay attention (and money) to my health- fruits and good natural protein sources. Also, I can find more time for my mental health.

Question: I have been selected in the SSC CGL. Can I pursue an LLB with a job?
Answer: Please go through the following rules for Study Leave as per CCS conduct rules: Study leave may be granted to a Government servant with due regard to the exigencies of public service to enable him to undergo, in or out of India, a special course of study consisting of higher studies or specialized training in a professional or a technical subject having a direct and close connection with the sphere of his duty. Study leave may also be granted- (i) for a course of training or study tour in which a Government servant may not attend a regular academic or semi-academic course if the course of training or the study tour is certified to be of definite advantage to Government from the point of view of public interest and is related to sphere of duties of the Government servant; and (ii) for the purpose of studies connected with the framework or background of public administration subject to the conditions that- (a) the particular study or study tour should be approved by the authority competent to grant leave; and (b) the Government servant should be required to submit, on his return, a full report on the work done by him while on study leave; (iii) for the studies which may not be closely or directly connected with the work of a Government servant, but which are capable of widening his mind in a manner likely to improve his abilities as a civil servant and to equip him better to collaborate with those employed in other branches of the public service. For most of the candidates, the para (iii) above will apply with regards to LLB. Bar Council of India does not recognize distance degree in LLB. This is the reason hardly any college would offer the degree in distance mode. It is easier to get permission to pursue higher education in distance mode. However, if you wish to pursue any course in regular mode, you have to go through the proper channel and avail study leave. Please go through extant rules in detail here.

Answer: No, I don’t think so. There are no “upper level” jobs as such in CGL that require any specialisation.
